The 9:52 PM "memory group is missing or empty": the restart's shutdown stops the desktop first, and an account's own programs still asking found the group empty, which turned the check off. Once the desktop was seen in its group during a start, an empty group now stays enforced, and refusals are not logged while shutting down (peer59_t.sh 12). The 9:48 PM refusal (Linux user 1000, not in the group) is the check working: the desktop's user outside the desktop (the websites' Chromium window is, by design); not reproduced in QEMU. Tests: qt/host/bootentry60_t.sh 14/14 (with the released 2026111620 rudolfd: 0a, 0b), bootfiles60_t.sh 8/8, esprepair60_t.sh 24/24, peer59_t.sh 23/23, listeners59_t.sh 16/16, setsearch59_t.js 13/13; qt/sb/t160b_t.py in QEMU (bootentry-check.yml): the release alone 12/12 (the failure: run 44032359372), with this tree's rudolfd, espcheck and bootfiles.sh 16/16 (run 44030675207). (The QEMU guest had no network: the release's boot image was given to the same espcheck repair from a disk.) docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.0: the first cellular release › After 1.6.0: the native desktop decision (added on 2026-11-12)
docs.t: (2026-11-13: the prototype moved into 1.5.9 as a third desktop engine, Native (test): docs/plan-1.5.9.md Part 12. Decided on 2026-11-13 after its measurements: native. The shell in 1.6.0 (Part 12 above), the apps in 2.0 (docs/plan-2.0.md). The reasoning below is kept as it was written.) Before the first phone (1.6.x), decide whether Rudolf OS's shell becomes native (drawn by its own program, not by a web engine). Not before 1.6.0: its work is mostly the system's (modems, the SIM, ARM64), its desktop parts (Messages, the taskbar's signal, Settings › Mobile network) are planned in the desktop page and would otherwise be built twice, and the web page runs the same on x86 and ARM64 while ARM64 is brought up.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.0: the first cellular release › After 1.6.0: the native desktop decision (added on 2026-11-12)
docs.t: What it rests on: the hidden-memory reading (docs/plan-memdebug.md) and the lighter desktop page (docs/plan-1.5.9.md Part 10), both measured on the Vivobook: Standard's and Lite's memory at idle before and after. The prototype: a small native shell (taskbar, wallpaper, window frames) in a Wayland compositor, with the apps still web pages loaded when opened, measured on the Vivobook and on the ARM64 computer: memory at idle, with Oracle open, and with a game; start-up time; battery at idle.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.0: the first cellular release › After 1.6.0: the native desktop decision (added on 2026-11-12)
docs.t: Then: if it saves enough on a 2 to 4 GB device, the phone's shell starts native, and the desktop can follow as Rudolf OS 2.0 (every app moved over, the browser build and the phone web app kept or retired). If not, the web desktop stays and the effort goes into slimming it further. For scale (2026-11-12): Standard at idle about 1.0 to 1.2 GB; light native Linux desktops (Xfce, LXQt) typically 300 to 500 MB for the whole system. The desktop is about 4.9 MB of code in 97 files: a native desktop rewrites all of it, so it is a release of its own, never part of another.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-15: "What items have been pushed beyond 1.6.0? Can they all be added to a plan for 1.6.1?" This plan gathers every item that docs/plan-1.6.0.md moved past 1.6.0, with where it came from, and (Parts 18 to 21, 2026-11-20) what was found since and not yet in a plan. Nothing here is built yet. The owner's rule for the native desktop holds for every part: "Rudolf OS on the native desktop should appear and function exactly as it does in Chromium mode."

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 1. Several monitors, on the three workspaces (from 1.6.0 Part 12, item 7)
docs.t: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-15: "Rudolf OS has three workspaces that can be selected in the bottom right of the taskbar. These workspaces will be the basis for Rudolf being able to support up to three monitors/displays, as well as having three panels for the mobile build that can be selected by swiping left/right similar to how Android phones work." Built after the 1.6.0 beta. Up to three displays, each showing one of the three workspaces, with its own wallpaper and taskbar. A window moved to another workspace moves to that display; the taskbar on each display lists that workspace's windows (as the taskbar lists the shown workspace's windows today).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 1. Several monitors, on the three workspaces (from 1.6.0 Part 12, item 7)
docs.t: One display: as today. The three workspaces are switched from the taskbar, Super+Ctrl+arrows and the menus. Standard and Native alike: rudolf-display gives Chromium one output today, so Standard needs the change too (decided by the owner, so the rule holds); Native follows RandR's outputs. Plugged in and out: a display unplugged takes its workspace back onto the remaining ones, with its windows; Settings › Display lists the displays and which workspace each shows. Tests: Xvfb with several screens (or Xephyr / RandR's virtual outputs) for both engines, compared with same_t.sh; on the Vivobook with an HDMI monitor (owner).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › The phone, split in two (owner, 2026-11-15)
docs.t: Decided on 2026-11-15, after asking whether the first real phone would be easier in 2.0 than in 1.6: "Make the sensible split." 2.0 brings the two things a phone people carry needs most, Wayland (touch gestures, rotation, scaling, the on-screen keyboard, power-saving drawing) and native apps (a fraction of the memory, so a day on the battery), but not the hardest part: making Rudolf OS run on one particular phone. So the phone comes in two stages:

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › The phone, split in two (owner, 2026-11-15)
docs.t: Stage 1, here in 1.6.1: the hardware. Rudolf OS boots on one ARM64 phone and its hardware works: the modem's data, texts and voice calls, emergency calls checked, the call's sound, sleep with the modem waking it, charging and the battery. It runs today's native desktop (X11) as it is: proving the hardware, not the phone's interface (Parts 2, 4, 6 and 7 below). Stage 2, in 2.0: the phone build. The phone's own interface on Wayland, the three swipe panels, and native apps laid out for touch, on the hardware stage 1 proved (docs/plan-2.0.md, "The phone build"). Nothing on a phone is flashed or unlocked without the owner's decision.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 2. The mobile build's three panels (from the same decision): the groundwork only
docs.t: The phone's home screen is the three workspaces as three panels, swiped left and right as on Android. In 1.6.1 only the groundwork: the workspaces' code from Part 1 written so a panel is a workspace shown full screen, and a horizontal swipe on a touch screen switching workspaces on both desktops (tested with a touch screen in QEMU and on the phone of Part 4). The phone's home screen itself, with its status bar, notification shade and app grid, is 2.0's phone build (stage 2).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 3. Lite, refined as a compatibility option (from 1.6.0 Part 15)
docs.t: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-15: Native replaces Lite as the desktop; Lite stays in Settings › System health › Desktop engine as a compatibility option, "to be worked on and refined later". Left from 1.5.8 and 1.5.9: the desktop's menus and windows behind Oracle's tab pages (the covered tab's still picture while a menu is open); stutter in Oracle's tabs; Google sign-in for GitHub (symptoms to be described first); GPU drawing for Lite measured; Oracle's WebKit tabs: YouTube, Google sign-in with FedCM, a download, full screen, memory with 5 tabs; the lock and sign-in screen settings and the shutting-down screen; the dynamic backgrounds' moving parts.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 4. The first phone, stage 1: the hardware (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0", and docs/plan-1.5.8.md 8.3)
docs.t: The phone's hardware made to work, on today's native desktop; its interface is 2.0's (stage 2). One well-supported phone first: a used PinePhone Pro (discontinued in August 2025, but its hardware is the best supported by mainline Linux and its modem, the Quectel EG25-G, has working VoLTE: Part 7), with the OnePlus 6/6T after it (its VoLTE does not work yet in postmarketOS). Bought and chosen by the owner.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 4. The first phone, stage 1: the hardware (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0", and docs/plan-1.5.8.md 8.3)
docs.t: Starting: the ARM64 release from 1.6.0's cellular and ARM64 plan (stage A in QEMU, stage B's first ARM64 computer), on the phone through its UEFI-capable boot firmware (Tow-Boot or U-Boot with UEFI on the PinePhone Pro), so it starts as Rudolf OS starts on a computer: the boot menu, Secure Boot where the firmware allows, recovery. The kernel: Rudolf's own build with the phone's drivers (the device tree and options postmarketOS and mainline Linux use for it, written into kconfig-arm64.sh), never a vendor kernel.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 4. The first phone, stage 1: the hardware (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0", and docs/plan-1.5.8.md 8.3)
docs.t: The modem: mobile data, texts and picture messages (1.6.0's Messages), voice calls (a call each way, hold, two calls, DTMF tones for menus), and emergency calls, which must be checked on each device and carrier before they are offered (Part 7 says how). A minimal call screen in today's desktop (answer, end, mute, speaker, keypad), enough to prove calls; the phone's real dialler is stage 2's. The call's sound: the earpiece, the speaker and a headset, with the modem's audio routed (ALSA UCM for the phone's sound card), the microphone, no echo.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 4. The first phone, stage 1: the hardware (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0", and docs/plan-1.5.8.md 8.3)
docs.t: Power: sleep with the modem waking the phone for a call or a text (and the alarm clock), the battery's level, charging and the charger's limit, the screen's brightness, the power key. The rest of the hardware, at driver level: the touch screen, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the cameras detected by libcamera, the sensors (accelerometer, proximity, light) and GPS readable, vibration. Their apps and behaviour (auto-rotation, the screen off at the ear, a Camera app) are stage 2's. Today's desktop on a phone screen: Native on X11, scaled for the screen, the on-screen keyboard (1.6.0's), touch mode: usable for testing, not meant to be a phone's interface.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 4. The first phone, stage 1: the hardware (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0", and docs/plan-1.5.8.md 8.3)
docs.t: Done when: the phone starts Rudolf OS from its storage, makes and takes a call on a T-Mobile-network SIM, sends and receives texts, sleeps and wakes for a call, and its standby battery drain is measured (Part 6), all written in docs/testing.md.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 4. The first phone, stage 1: the hardware (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0", and docs/plan-1.5.8.md 8.3)
docs.t: On 1.6's kernel and X11 (2026-11-20): stage 1 is built on 1.6.x (the 6.18 LTS, X11, ARM64); the phone's own build and interface move to 2.0's "next" channel (the newest kernel, Wayland). A phone with 8 GB for the full desktop and Wayland testing: the OnePlus 6T (8 GB), Snapdragon 845 as the OnePlus 6, started through U-Boot's UEFI from its boot partition; its VoLTE (needed for calls on T-Mobile) does not work yet, so the PinePhone Pro stays the phone for calls. The Fairphone 5 (8 GB) to watch as its mainline support matures. Phones running on Android's drivers (Furi Labs FLX1s+, Volla Phone Quintus) do not fit "never a vendor kernel".

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 4. The first phone, stage 1: the hardware (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0", and docs/plan-1.5.8.md 8.3)
docs.t: Nothing on a phone is flashed or unlocked without the owner's decision.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 5. eSIM and 5G (from 1.6.0 "Not in 1.6.0")
docs.t: eSIM provisioning (downloading a carrier's eSIM profile); 5G standalone features beyond what the modem does by itself. 1.6.0 left these without a release; they are here so they are not lost. They need hardware with an eSIM and a 5G modem.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 6. Closing the gap with Android (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-15, after comparing 1.6.1 with Android: the items that decide whether someone could carry a Rudolf phone every day. Each is measured on the first phone (Part 4) and compared with the same phone on Android where it can be. Split (owner, 2026-11-15): 1.6.1 does what the hardware decides (marked *1.6.1* below: the measurements, calls with the carrier, the modem's sleep); the parts people use every day are 2.0's phone build (marked *2.0*), since they are built on Wayland and the native apps.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 6. Closing the gap with Android (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: *2.0, measured in 1.6.1.* Android apps through Waydroid, made dependable: set up from Settings, apps from F-Droid and an app store the owner chooses, their windows and notifications in Rudolf's own; a list of apps that work and that refuse (banking apps that check the device), kept in the docs. Measured on the Vivobook first (docs/plan-1.6.0.md: "Waydroid measured on the Vivobook with Lite before it is offered").

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 6. Closing the gap with Android (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: *1.6.1 measured and the modem's sleep; the rest 2.0.* Battery life: the phone's idle and screen-on drain measured, then: the modem, Wi-Fi and the screen put to sleep when not needed, suspend with the modem waking it for a call or a text, apps in the background held back as Android's Doze does; targets set from the measurements, shown in Settings › Battery. *1.6.1.* Calls with the carrier: voice calls over 4G (VoLTE) where the modem and carrier allow, Wi-Fi calling if the carrier offers it, a call to a real phone and an emergency-call check on each device (Part 4), the call's sound through the earpiece, speaker and a headset.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 6. Closing the gap with Android (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: *2.0 (the cameras detected in 1.6.1).* The camera: photos and video with the phone's cameras (libcamera), in a Camera app; quality compared with Android's on the same phone. *2.0 (readable in 1.6.1).* The phone's sensors and hardware: auto-rotation, proximity (the screen off at the ear), brightness, GPS for maps and weather, the fingerprint reader where the phone has one, vibration. *2.0.* Messaging apps people need: what works through Waydroid or the web (Signal, WhatsApp Web), and what does not, said plainly in the docs. Tests: each measured and written in docs/testing.md; the battery and call results on the owner's phone and carrier.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 7. T-Mobile and the prepaid services on its network (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-15: "Plan for T-Mobile and adjacent prepaid service coverage in 1.6.1." The US has no 3G left, so calls need VoLTE, and carriers decide which phones get it. T-Mobile's network is the friendliest to Linux phones (reports in the Pine64 wiki's carrier list and forum, 2020 to 2024); AT&T and Verizon are later. The carriers covered: T-Mobile (postpaid and prepaid), Mint Mobile, Tello, US Mobile on its T-Mobile network, Simple Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, Ultra Mobile and Google Fi (data and calls; Fi's first activation needs an Android phone and its picture messages do not work: said in Settings). The list is checked again before work starts, since prepaid brands change networks.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 7. T-Mobile and the prepaid services on its network (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: The first phone: the PinePhone Pro (Part 4). Its modem (Quectel EG25-G) has working VoLTE; the OnePlus 6's VoLTE does not work yet in postmarketOS (pmaports issue 1878), so it waits. Set up by itself: Settings › Mobile network recognises the carrier from the SIM (its MCC/MNC and its name) and fills in the APN exactly, letters' case included (US Mobile's "PWG" failed in lowercase on a PinePhone Pro; Simple Mobile's is "Simple"), with the picture messages' settings (MMSC, proxy). The APNs come from the operators' database 1.6.0 already ships, with Rudolf's own corrections for these carriers kept beside it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 7. T-Mobile and the prepaid services on its network (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: VoLTE turned on: the modem's IMS/VoLTE set up for T-Mobile (its carrier profile on the EG25-G), checked after every start and after a SIM change; Settings says whether calls go over 4G. Wi-Fi calling where T-Mobile offers it on the phone (VoWiFi through the modem's IMS), else said plainly. Texts and picture messages: SMS (1.6.0 Part 6) and MMS through the APN's MMSC, in the Messages app. Activation help: what each carrier needs (activate online, the phone's IMEI given to the carrier, support asked to turn VoLTE on for the line), written in the docs and linked from Settings when the SIM has no service.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 7. T-Mobile and the prepaid services on its network (added on 2026-11-15)
docs.t: 5G: not on the PinePhone Pro (an LTE modem). T-Mobile's 5G is tested later with a 5G modem card in a laptop (Part 5). Tests: a prepaid Mint or Tello SIM first (cheap, no contract), then T-Mobile itself: data, a call each way, a call to and from a landline, an emergency-call check as Part 4 says, texts and picture messages each way, Wi-Fi calling, roaming off, the APN filled in from a fresh SIM, and a call during a weak signal. Results in docs/testing.md, with the carrier and date. A host test of the APN table (each carrier's MCC/MNC and name gives the right APN, case kept). Later: AT&T's network (stricter about devices), then Verizon (approved phones only).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 8. Mobile data and the SIM on real hardware (moved from 1.6.0 on 2026-11-16)
docs.t: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-16: "For now, move the mobile/SIM testing to 1.6.1." 1.6.0 ships the cellular work proven without hardware (its stage A: ModemManager, Settings › Mobile network, the connection and failover, data and the monthly limit, the taskbar's signal, Messages, all with host, browser and QEMU tests against a stand-in modem); what needs a real modem and SIM is checked here, before 1.6.1's phone work relies on it. From docs/plan-1.6.0.md's stage B (items 1 to 3) and its release checks:

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 8. Mobile data and the SIM on real hardware (moved from 1.6.0 on 2026-11-16)
docs.t: The MiFi 7730L with an active SIM (the owner's choice; the HP desktop user's USB stick only if it is lent again): found in Settings › Network › Cellular modems (maker, model, SIM, operator), no "Invalid rule match" in /run/rudolf/modem.log, the self-test's modem line; the SIM's PIN (never the PUK on a SIM someone needs); the APN filled in (a prepaid T-Mobile-network SIM, Part 7); connected; Wi-Fi failover and back; IPv4 sites on an IPv6-only network (the CLAT); data counted against the operator's own count; the 80 % notice and data off at 100 %; an update offered on mobile data with its size; the bars and type against the device's own; the SIM taken out while running; unplugged and plugged in again; sleep and wake (after 1.6.0's sleep fix for the Vivobook, CONFIG_AMD_PMC).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 8. Mobile data and the SIM on real hardware (moved from 1.6.0 on 2026-11-16)
docs.t: Messages to and from a real phone (Unicode, a long one, the delivery report), a sign-in code, the notice with the desktop locked, kept across a restart and in the encrypted folder. Share this connection with the MiFi's USB tethering as the uplink (1.5.9 Part 4, waiting since then for a data plan). The FCC-unlock path on a laptop with a WWAN card (a used ThinkPad with a Fibocom L850-GL or Quectel EM05-G). Each checked on Standard and Native (the owner's rule), results in docs/testing.md with the carrier and date.

docs.t: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-16: "USB printers and ARM64 can be delayed until 1.6.1." USB printers back in 1.6.0 (owner, 2026-11-17): "Skip the test and just add it. Users can still print if the USB printing has issues and we can refine it in 1.6.1 with the data that comes back if it does." docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5)
docs.t: The aim: every operation that needs root moves into a small helper program that rudolfd runs with checked arguments; rudolfd drops to the rudolf user (uid 1000) once it has started and opened what it must. The areas (one PR each, in this order, each keeping the API byte for byte): drives (mount, unmount, eject, format, the encrypted home's unlock), updates (rudolf-update's slots, roll back, tostable: much is already a separate program), accounts (the per-account Linux users of 1.6.0 Part 10: useradd, chown, the keyring), power (restart, shut down, sleep, brightness), network (Wi-Fi, the firewall, the hostname), packages (rpk, Flatpak's system parts), and whatever a sweep for root-only calls finds (/sys writes, /dev access, mount, kill of others' processes).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5)
docs.t: Each helper: one job, its arguments validated again inside it (never trusting rudolfd), callable only by rudolfd (the rudolf user, checked by SO_PEERCRED on a root-owned socket, or a setuid helper owned root:rudolf mode 4750, whichever the area suits), logged, and small enough to read in one sitting. Never: a weaker check than today's (the token, the peer check of 1.5.9, administrator prompts), or a change the page or the native desktop can see.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: One broker, rudolf-rootd, which starts rudolfd (iso/sys/rudolf-rootd.c). rudolf-init runs `rudolf-rootd /usr/bin/rudolfd: it makes a socket pair, starts rudolfd with one end (RUDOLF_ROOTD_FD`; rudolfd makes it close-on-exec at once) and keeps the other. It listens on nothing: no socket in the file system, no port. For a request rudolfd makes a socket pair of its own and passes one end over that first one; rudolf-rootd then checks who made it (SO_PEERCRED: root, or rudolf (1000) once rudolfd drops to it; and that process's /proc/PID/exe is the program it started), reads one message on it (RRQ1, the helper's name, its arguments, each ending in a zero byte, and three descriptors: the helper's standard input, output and error; iso/sys/rudolf-root.h) and runs /usr/lib/rudolf/root/NAME with exactly those arguments (execve, never a shell), with an empty environment (only PATH), its working folder /, umask 022, every other descriptor closed and every signal back to its default; it answers with four bytes, the exit status (254 refused, 253 not started). An unknown name, a malformed message, a request from another user or another program is refused and said in the health log (Security).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: Why not the socket in the file system checked by SO_PEERCRED and /proc/PID/exe (the first idea): once rudolfd runs as uid 1000, any program of that user can start its own copy of /usr/bin/rudolfd with LD_PRELOAD, or trace one (not set-user-ID, so the user's own), and that copy's /proc/PID/exe is rudolfd too: the check would let it in. The descriptor handed over at rudolfd's start cannot be had that way: rudolfd is not traceable by the user (it becomes non-dumpable when it drops; PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 is set explicitly in the drop's step), and nothing it starts inherits the descriptor. The exe check is kept as a second line (a descriptor leaked by mistake still lets nothing else in).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: Why not set-user-ID helpers (root:rudolf 4750): every process of the group could run them (the desktop's browser is uid 1000 too), with whatever environment, descriptors, limits and working folder it chooses (the classic set-user-ID mistakes), and rudolfd could not set no_new_privs (it stops set-user-ID). One broker gives every area the same check in one place, a clean start for each helper, and leaves no_new_privs possible. No area needs set-user-ID, so every area uses the broker. The cost: one more small root process, which parses only fixed messages from rudolfd.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: Each helper is a program of its own (root:root 0700 in a folder of root's, 0755; never set-user-ID), one area, small enough to read in one sitting. It checks every argument again itself, whatever rudolfd checked: device names letters and digits only and ones the kernel has (/sys/class/block, /sys/block for whole disks); paths made canonical (realpath: no "..", every link followed) and kept inside their allowed root (a link out of it is refused), files plain (not a link) and owned by the desktop's user or the signed-in account's user (another account's file, or a hard link to one, is refused); account names from the account list (/persist/etc/rudolf/account-users), never from rudolfd's word alone; keys and passwords on standard input, never as arguments (anyone can read a process's arguments); the scripts it hands work to are run with argument lists, never a command line for a shell. A refusal is said in the health log (Security), as is anything that erases or rewrites a disk; routine actions (mount, unmount) are not, to keep the log readable. rr_health writes the health log's format ({"t","k","m"}).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: rudolfd's side (iso/sys/rudolfd-root.inc): root_call (the helper's status, as run() gave a command's), root_run, root_out (its output, as run_out(), read while it runs), root_job (as start_job: job.name, job.log, job.status). Started without rudolf-rootd (an older rudolf-init, or the QEMU tests that start rudolfd again by hand) and running as root, rudolfd runs the helper itself in the same clean way; so every step works whether or not the drop is on, and the API is the same byte for byte either way (the host test compares them).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: The drop (the last step, behind a switch until every area has moved, default off): rudolfd starts as root (from rudolf-rootd), does what must be done before (opens 127.0.0.1:8080, which needs no root as a port above 1023; reads the start-up facts; makes RUN/d, its own folder, rudolf's 0700, for the files it writes; the health log made rudolf's 0600: the helpers still append to it as root), then setgroups to rudolf's own groups (audio and video for the screenshot of /dev/fb0), setresgid and setresuid to 1000, checks it cannot go back (setuid(0) fails), and sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0. No capabilities are kept (none is needed: binding 8080 does not need one, reading /proc/net/tcp and the desktop's own processes' descriptors for the peer check of 15.1 is allowed to the same user). The switch: a build flag (RUDOLFD_DROP) and, for testing, rudolf.rudolfd_drop=1 on the start-up options; the default turns on only when every area of 11.1 has moved and the QEMU checks pass with it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: no_new_privs: rudolfd sets it after the drop if nothing it starts still needs set-user-ID. Today two would: su (the clipboard: unneeded once rudolfd is the desktop's user) and Chromium's chrome_sandbox (4755) for the windows rudolfd starts (websites on Lite, Tor windows); with no_new_privs Chromium cannot use it and needs its namespace sandbox, which needs unprivileged user namespaces. So: no_new_privs is set on rudolfd itself only if the QEMU checks show Chromium's windows still start with it; otherwise those windows are started through a helper and no_new_privs is set in every other child rudolfd starts (prctl in the child before exec). rudolf-rootd's helpers are unaffected either way (they are rudolf-rootd's children, not rudolfd's).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 11. rudolfd's root work split into helpers (added on 2026-11-16; from docs/plan-1.5.9.md 15.5) › 11.2 The design (2026-11-17)
docs.t: The accounts' files after the drop: rudolfd as uid 1000 cannot read /persist/accounts/ID (the account's user's, 0700), and giving it a capability to (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE) would undo the point. So the accounts' area adds a file service run as the account's own user (not root): started by rudolf-rootd at the unlock with the account's folder, serving the home/* operations over a socket pair to rudolfd (the same openat(O_NOFOLLOW) walk as rudolfd-home.inc today, moved). rudolfd's API stays as it is.

docs.t: Updates (2026-11-17, branch root-helpers-update, after root-helpers-drives): the updates helper (iso/sys/rudolf-updates.c, /usr/lib/rudolf/root/updates): every rudolf-update command rudolfd ran (check, download, rollback, stable-info, to-stable, status, speedtest, boot-ok, return-official keep|erase, set url|auto|channel, developer on|off), the arguments checked again as rudolfd checks them (the beta address only through set channel beta; a developer's key 44 characters of base64; addresses without spaces or quotes), and the desktop's page update (POST update, the page on standard input; POST rollback). Found and kept as they were: POST rollback always answers "returned to the previous version" (the old command's status was sync's); the page update is not signed (any holder of the token can replace the desktop's page until a restart) and Developer mode and Return to official are asked an administrator's password by the page only, not by rudolfd: for the owner (the accounts step can move the administrator's check into the helpers, the password on standard input).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 12. Kernel tuning (added on 2026-11-16; proposed on 2026-11-12)
docs.t: The kernel already has zram (zstd), MGLRU, PSI, schedutil and the AMD and Intel P-state drivers (iso/kconfig.sh). What is left is measured, not guessed: each change kept only if the numbers say so. Responsiveness: PREEMPT_DYNAMIC with preempt=full against the current default; HZ 1000 against 250; measured as the desktop's input lag (the page's lag meter, rudolf-native's frame times) while a build or a game loads the CPU. AMD power: amd_pstate=active with an energy-performance preference (balance_performance on mains, balance_power on battery), set by the power settings; measured as battery drain at idle and with a video.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 12. Kernel tuning (added on 2026-11-16; proposed on 2026-11-12)
docs.t: Start-up time: what loads before "the desktop was ready" (built-in drivers that could be modules, the initramfs's size, waits in rudolf-init); the health log's timings (1.6.0, #425) are the measure. The Vivobook takes 27 to 37 s. Memory: vm.swappiness and zram's size with Oracle, a game and a call at once on 3.3 GB. How: QEMU first for what QEMU can show (start-up, memory), a test kernel built with each choice; the Vivobook last, by the owner (battery and real input lag), with a short checklist of numbers to note on each kernel.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 12. Kernel tuning (added on 2026-11-16; proposed on 2026-11-12)
docs.t: One kernel for every computer, so a second machine (owner, 2026-11-16): Rudolf OS ships one x86-64 kernel, so a change tuned on the Vivobook must not make another PC slower or stop it starting. Every change is also checked on the owner's Asus desktop (RuckXTrauma), running Rudolf OS live from a USB stick (never installed there, nothing on its disk changed): kept only if it helps on at least one machine and hurts on neither. Its specifications go here from its System report: CPU and cores ___, memory ___, graphics ___, storage ___. On it, power is measured as responsiveness and temperatures or fan noise (no battery). Start-up is also checked in QEMU on several kinds of virtual hardware (q35 and i440fx; AHCI, NVMe, virtio-blk, USB storage; BIOS and UEFI): anything a computer needs to reach its root file system stays built in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 12. Kernel tuning (added on 2026-11-16; proposed on 2026-11-12)
docs.t: First, before any tuning is merged: the kernel's required features checked at build time (owner, 2026-11-16). Tuning must never remove a feature programs depend on. iso/kconfig.sh already stops the build when some groups are missing (the memory options, sound, games, Thunderbolt); it is widened to every feature Rudolf OS's programs and security rely on, each listed with who needs it, so a tuning change that drops one fails the build instead of reaching a computer: - Flatpak and bubblewrap: user, PID, network, mount and IPC namespaces; seccomp and its filters; overlayfs; FUSE (the document portal). - The Debian container and Wine: namespaces, cgroups v2 and its controllers (cpu, memory, io, pids), binfmt_misc, 32-bit programs (IA32_EMULATION) for Wine and Steam. - The desktop and its sandboxes: cgroups for the desktop's memory group (rudolfd's peer check), inotify, epoll, eventfd, signalfd, timerfd, memfd, the X server's needs (DRM, KMS, DRI3's file passing), uinput, evdev. - Security: Secure Boot's kernel lockdown, module signature checking, YAMA, the keyring (KEYS), the encrypted home's dm-crypt and its ciphers, the firewall (nftables), audit if used. - Storage and start-up: every disk controller and file system needed to reach the system disk (AHCI, NVMe, virtio, USB storage, SquashFS, ext4,

docs.t: vfat for the EFI partition), the initramfs's needs. - Power and devices: suspend (s2idle), AMD_PMC, the P-state drivers, CPU frequency, thermal, the battery. The list is made by reading what each program needs (bubblewrap's and Flatpak's documented requirements, rudolfd's, the X server's), and checked against today's kernel so it starts green. Its test: a deliberately broken configuration (one option removed from each group) must fail the build with that option's name and who needs it. This check is its own PR, merged before any of Part 12's tuning PRs.

Swappiness: 60 is clearly worse (twice the stalls, and the guard in critical twice as long), which confirms 1.5.9's move to a high value; 100, 180 and 200 differ by less than the runs among themselves (180's call figure ran 50 to 241): 180 is kept. zram's size: 1.5 × memory changed nothing measurable (zram never filled at 1 ×): kept as it is.

docs.t: lz4: fewer late call periods in all three pairs, fewer slow game frames in two (the third even), fewer stalls in two, and the guard critical less than half as long: lz4 is faster to compress and read back. But it packs less (about 2:1 against zstd's 3:1), so zram holds less before memory really runs out, which these 100-second runs did not reach and on 3.3 GB matters (the Vivobook's game was ended by the guard in 1.5.9). Not changed yet: a later PR would build ZRAM_BACKEND_LZ4 and let the memory setting choose it, once a run as long as a real game session shows it does not end processes sooner.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 13. Files dropped from outside onto the native desktop (added on 2026-11-16; 1.6.0 Part 12's known differences)
docs.t: On Standard a file dragged from a Linux app (the Debian file manager, a Flatpak) onto the desktop is saved in the Desktop folder. rudolf-native did not speak X11's drag and drop (XDND), so such drops did nothing on Native. **Built on 2026-11-17 (PR #444, "files dropped from outside onto the native desktop"). Merged early, and kept in 1.6.0 by the owner's decision of 2026-11-16 ("Keep it in 1.6.0"): it ships with 1.6.0, not 1.6.1.**

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 13. Files dropped from outside onto the native desktop (added on 2026-11-16; 1.6.0 Part 12's known differences)
docs.t: What Standard does, checked in its page and in Chromium (xdrop161_std.js): a file dropped anywhere on the desktop goes into the Desktop folder, also over a folder's icon or the Trash (their own drop handlers take only the page's own drags; the drop then reaches the desktop's: shell25.js), named as the page names files (upper case, NAME - COPY.EXT on a clash), kept as text or as a data: URL by its type, over 64 MB refused ("Too large"); dropped text (no file) is refused; the taskbar takes no drop and raises no window. Native now does exactly that. The plan's "plain text as a note" and "a hover raises the window" were not Standard's, so Native does neither (the rule); a raise on hover would be new on both engines, for the owner to decide.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 13. Files dropped from outside onto the native desktop (added on 2026-11-16; 1.6.0 Part 12's known differences)
docs.t: Native: the desktop is an X drop target (XDND 5, GTK's): copy while a drag offering text/uri-list is over it and an account is signed in (not locked, not the guest), refused for text; the file:// paths go to a page of the shell's (#app=do-fs&op=xdrop, oneapp59.js oaXdrop), which does shell25.js's drop line by line (the same names, checks and secIngress), reading each file through rudolfd; XdndFinished (copy) once the page has kept them. Drops take their turn (one page at a time). The paths travel in parts of at most 12 000 characters.

docs.t: The owner, 2026-11-18, on Native with Steam, Discord and Claude open: "Steam, Discord, Claude, and other apps installed from Debian, Flatpak, and some source sites seem to use their own windows inside of the OS-based windows. Is there a way to have non-Rudolf apps like these use only Rudolf's own windows and title bars?" Of the three ways offered, the owner chose the suggested mix ("We will go with your suggestion"):

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 15. One title bar for apps that draw their own (added on 2026-11-18)
docs.t: Why there are two. Electron and Chromium apps (Discord, Claude, Steam's new interface, VS Code, Chromium-based browsers) draw their own title bar and ask the window manager for none (_MOTIF_WM_HINTS, decorations 0). rudolf-native frames every window the same, so it adds Rudolf's above theirs. Their bar is more than a title: Steam's menus (Steam, View, Friends, Games, Help) and its account button, Discord's inbox and help buttons and the "Direct Messages" heading. Moving the window by dragging their bar, and their own minimize, maximize and close buttons, need from the window manager what rudolf-native does not do yet: _NET_WM_MOVERESIZE (it moves and resizes for the app), _NET_WM_STATE_MAXIMIZED_VERT and _HORZ, _NET_FRAME_EXTENTS. Standard frames no Linux app's window (rudolf-display shows them without a title bar of Rudolf's), so this part is Native's.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 15. One title bar for apps that draw their own (added on 2026-11-18)
docs.t: 1. The app's own setting first: Rudolf's title bar, nothing lost. Where an app can use the system's title bar, Rudolf asks it to, once, the first time it starts it, and only when the person has not chosen otherwise in the app: Chromium-based browsers (Flathub's Chromium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi; Debian's Chromium): their "Use system title bar and borders" (browser.custom_chrome_frame: false in the profile's Preferences, when the key is not there yet); VS Code and VSCodium: window.titleBarStyle: native (when not set);

Those windows then ask for decorations, and get Rudolf's title bar as any other. 2. Otherwise, the app's own bar alone (the default). A window asking for no decorations gets no title bar of Rudolf's: its frame keeps the edge (1 px, or 2 px with high contrast), the round corners and the resize edges; the taskbar button, Alt+Tab, the overview, the workspaces, snapping and the LitePoint transitions (1.6.0 Part 17) all as before. For its own bar to work, rudolf-native does what such apps ask:

Games and Wine's borderless windows (the same hint, a window the size of the screen) stay as they are: full screen.

With Rudolf's, the app's own bar is cut away as Oracle's Chromium bar is (the clip window and its insets, 1.5.9 12.3c), at a height known for that app (the list above, cut entries: the bar's height in the app's pixels at 100 %, scaled as the app is). Offered only for apps on the list, whose bar holds only what Rudolf's has (the title and the three buttons); for one whose bar has more (Steam's menus, Discord's buttons), the menu says what would be lost instead of offering it. docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Moved to 1.6.0 (the owner, 2026-11-19: "All four into 1.6.0"; one beta when all are built). Built there; this text stays the plan. The owner, 2026-11-19: "The version made on the stick and the repository that updates are checked for should come from whatever the set update address is written as by the computer's admin-level user. The system should be able to check that the set update repository is set-up/working correctly and that it is able to match the user's key to it. The intent is for people to be able to roll out their own updates but only to computers that are running the key specific to their own version/build of Rudolf OS. USB sticks pull directly from whatever the set update address is, and still checks to ensure it is set up properly before it attempts to make a copy of that repository's version of Rudolf OS. This is intended for people to be able to download and use each-other's builds." Decided the same day: sticks offer both (the address first, "This Rudolf OS" kept for use without internet); another key's build is allowed on a stick after a warning; Get beta versions keeps the repository that is

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: set. How it is today. Check for updates uses the Update address box (update.conf url), else the build's own default (/etc/rudolf/update-url). An update installs only when its release list is signed by a key the running system trusts (the build's rpk-keys, plus Developer mode's extra-keys): that part of the intent is already true and stays as it is. But Get beta versions overwrites the box with the build's own …/beta (and …/stable when turned off); nothing says whether an address works before an update fails; and Make a USB stick never downloads: it copies the running system (or an image already in Downloads), its boot files from the running release's own boot.iso.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: 1. Check this address. A button by the Update address box (and the same check when Save is pressed, and in rudolf-update check-url URL, for rudolfd's sys/urlcheck). Each line passes, warns or fails, in plain words: the address answers, with manifest.txt and manifest.sig (https only, as today); it is a Rudolf OS release list this computer can read (its format, datafmt/readsfmt), not expired; whose key signed it: this computer's (the official key, or Developer mode's key) → "Updates from this address install here"; another key → "This is another build of Rudolf OS, signed with key xxxx… (its fingerprint): updates from it do not install on this computer. You can make a USB stick from it.";

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: that other key is the build's own: the list's signature verifies with a key in that release's own base layer (/etc/rudolf/rpk-keys, read from base.sfs after its checksum matches the list), so a list that its own system would refuse is reported as broken, not as "another build"; every file the list names, and the release's boot.iso beside its vmlinuz, can be downloaded (sizes checked by a request for the first byte, nothing big downloaded);

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: its other channel: …/beta beside …/stable (a warning only when missing: the beta switch then has nowhere to go). Saving an address signed with another key asks first: "Updates will stop on this computer until the address is changed back." The status line under Update and recovery says which key the set address uses. 2. Get beta versions keeps the repository. On: the set address's …/beta; off: its …/stable (and the "leaving the betas" rule, tostable, as today). An address that does not end in /stable or /beta is used as it is, and the switch says so. Developer mode's own address is unchanged.

docs.t: 3. Make a USB stick from the update address. "Rudolf OS to put on it" lists first "The latest from the update address (Rudolf OS *version*, *serial*)", then "This Rudolf OS" and the images in Downloads as today. Before anything is erased: the check of item 1 for that address (all must pass; a warning about the other channel is fine) and room on RUDOLFDATA for the download.

docs.t: Downloaded to /persist/os/stickdl/SERIAL/: the release list and its signature, boot.iso, every layer; each layer's SHA-256 must match the list (layers this computer already has with the same checksum are linked, not downloaded); the boot image's kernel must be the list's vmlinuz; the list's signature must verify with the release's own key (item 1).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Another key's build: before the drive is erased, a warning names it ("another build of Rudolf OS, signed with key xxxx…, from ADDRESS"), says that it gets its updates from its own maker, not from this computer's, that with Secure Boot on it starts only where its maker's Secure Boot key is trusted, and that its Recovery mode is the official Rudolf OS (item 4); the administrator confirms. mkstick.sh writes boot.iso as the image (as with an image from Downloads) and puts the release in the stick's RUDOLFDATA system slot, with that release's own update address (the one it came from), so the stick updates from its maker. "Also copy my files and settings" stays available.

docs.t: The downloads are kept until the next stick is made from another release (one release only), so a second stick needs no second download. The stick check (mkstick.sh --check) and Storage's line about a plugged-in stick name the build's key when it is not this computer's.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: 4. Recovery mode is always the official build's newest stable release. The owner, 2026-11-19: "Recovery Mode boot is always locked to the official build's most recent stable version. This is so that if someone encounters a catastrophic failure of their normal boot that they have a reliable and guaranteed way to recover their machine." Today the start-up side already holds: the boot menu's Recovery mode (recovery.efi, its own small initramfs with the official key alone) starts only a system/r whose list the official key signed, whatever the update address or Developer mode. What is missing:

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Kept newest. rudolf-update fetches the official recovery system once (recovery-fetch) and never again. Each update check (whatever the address) also reads the official stable list (OFFICIAL_URL, the official key alone); when its serial is newer than system/r's, the new one is downloaded beside it (r.new, the layers system/r already has linked), checked, and swapped in at once, with recovery.efi from that release's boot.iso; the old one stays until the new one is complete. Not while in recovery mode, and never from the update address, a beta, or Developer mode's key.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: On every stick. Today a stick's rescue slot is a copy of the stick's own system (os_rescue). Instead, whatever the stick's system (this Rudolf OS, an image, the update address, another person's build): its system/r is the official newest stable (this computer's own when it is that, else downloaded and checked as above) and its recovery.efi is the official one. A stick is not made without it ("Connect to the internet: a stick always gets the official recovery system").

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Another person's build cannot replace it. Its boot files may bring their own rudolf.efi, but recovery.efi is always the official one (bootfiles.sh and install.sh keep the official file; the start-up file check of 1.6.0 Part 15 reports any other); and its updates never write system/r. Settings › Update and recovery says which official release Recovery mode starts, and when it was last renewed. What does not change. Updates never install across keys. "Return to official" keeps using the official address. "New boot files" (Secure Boot) keeps its own image choice, with the official recovery.efi beside it. Built in 1.6.0 (2026-11-19), and where it differs from the text above.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: rudolf-update check-url URL (JSON), through rudolf-updates and rudolfd sys/urlcheck; Settings › Update and recovery › Update address: Check this address, and Save checks first, asks before an address whose updates would not install here, and sends an administrator's name and password (rudolfd now refuses the address without them: "written by the computer's admin-level user"). Files are checked with HEAD requests.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Whose key, for another build: an Ed25519 signature does not name its key, so each channel now publishes its build's public key beside its list (key.txt, rudolf-release.yml); the check names that key when it signs the list, and says the address is set up wrong when no key there does. Reading the key out of the release's base layer is done when a stick is made (it needs the layer downloaded), as item 3 says. Get beta versions: chan_url (the set address's /beta or /stable; neither: kept, and said).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: rudolf-update stick-fetch URL DIR; Make a USB stick's "The latest from the update address" (@address: rudolfd, rudolf-drives, mkstick.sh): /persist/os/stickdl, checked with the release's own key (its base layer's rpk-keys, kept as keys for install.sh's check of its boot image), the official recovery system beside it, and the stick's update address the one it came from. Settings checks the address first and names another build before the erase question.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 16. Each other's builds: the update address decides the updates and the sticks (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Recovery mode: recovery-fetch replaces an older official recovery system with the newest official stable release (looked at, detached, at most once a day from each update check); os_rescue gives every stick the official recovery system (this computer's, brought up to date, or downloaded), and only without one (offline, none here) a rescue copy of its own system, with a warning, rather than no stick (the owner chose to keep sticks that need no internet). status says which release Recovery mode starts, shown in Settings.

docs.t: The official recovery.efi on a stick made from another build (done 2026-11-19, the owner: "Add items 1 and 2 to the next scheduled beta build"). Its boot image brings its maker's recovery.efi, which checks the recovery system with its maker's key. os_recefi (oscopy.sh, run by mkstick.sh once the stick has the official recovery system) puts the official recovery.efi of slot r's own release in its place, in the stick's EFI system partition: from the boot image beside that release (its address from r's signed list), its checksum and Rudolf OS's Secure Boot signature checked; kept in os/recefi for the next stick; the boot menu's Recovery mode entry added when the build has none. The build's own start is left. Never fatal: offline with none kept, a warning. With Secure Boot on, the official file starts where the computer trusts Rudolf OS's key (another build's own shim may not). Test: iso/qt/host/recefi60_t.sh (12).

docs.t: Moved to 1.6.0 (the owner, 2026-11-19: "All four into 1.6.0"; one beta when all are built). Built there; this text stays the plan. The owner, 2026-11-19, after "Can two-factor authenticated menu sign-in be enabled from the security settings?": "Plan the proper version." Decided the same day: hardware security keys and authenticator-app codes (not phone passkeys); an administrator's copy of an account's key stays, and the person may turn it off; an administrator may require a second step for administrators or for every account.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: How it is today. User Settings › Sign-in options › "Add a security key or passkey…" (settings25.js, WebAuthn): the desktop page checks the key's signature after the password. It guards the sign-in screen only: the account's file key (fk) is opened by the password alone (PBKDF2, ks), so a copy of the disk needs only the password; the check is the page's, not the system's; Native and Lite refuse such an account (desktop/accounts key); there is one key and no backup; no authenticator codes. 1. Hardware security keys, read by the system (all three engines).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: rudolfd talks to FIDO2 keys itself (USB and NFC readers; libfido2 loaded with dlopen, as OpenSSL is, from the base layer; /dev/hidraw* for rudolfd only), so Standard, Native and Lite, the lock screen and remote access (rudolf-remote) use the same check. Not the browser's WebAuthn: WebKit and the native shell have none that can do item 2.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Adding one (User Settings › Sign-in options › Security keys › Add): password first, then touch the key (and its PIN, if it has one: asked on screen, never kept). Each account may have up to 5, with names ("Blue YubiKey"); the screen asks for a second one as a spare ("If you lose your only key, only a recovery code or an administrator can let you in"). Signing in: password, then "Touch your security key" (any of the account's). A key with a PIN asks for it (the key counts wrong PINs itself and locks after 8).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: 2. The key unlocks the files, not only the screen. For an account with a security key, its file key is no longer wrapped by the password alone: each security key gets its own copy of fk, wrapped with HKDF-SHA-256(password key ‖ the key's hmac-secret output for this account's salt) (FIDO2 hmac-secret: the key computes it inside, from a secret that never leaves it). The password-only copy is deleted (and overwritten) when the first key is added. So a copy of the disk, with the password, opens nothing without one of the keys. The same goes for accounts' copies. Keys that cannot do hmac-secret (very old U2F-only ones) are refused when added, with that reason.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: A recovery code (24 letters and digits in 6 groups, shown once, "write it down or print it") is one more copy of fk, wrapped with the code (PBKDF2, 600 000 rounds). It signs in without a key once, then asks to add a key or make a new code. Administrators' copies (a.ak, 1.5.0) stay, on by default: an administrator can still open the account's files and reset its password (the person's keys are then removed: they add them again). The person can turn them off (User Settings › Sign-in options: "Administrators can open my files", as now), after a warning: "If you lose your keys and your recovery code, nobody can open your files."

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: 3. Authenticator-app codes (TOTP). Six-digit codes every 30 seconds from an app (Google or Microsoft Authenticator, Aegis, 2FAS, …). Adding: a QR code and the text secret, then a code to confirm. Signing in: password, then the code (one step either side of now accepted; a code used once is not taken again). Codes guard the sign-in only: the secret is kept wrapped by the account's password key, so it cannot add anything to the encryption, and Settings says so ("A security key also protects your files if the disk is copied; a code does not."). An account may have a security key, codes, or both (either one is enough at sign-in).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: 4. The system decides, not the page. Every sign-in goes through rudolfd (desktop/login, as Native's does now): the password, then the second step, then the file key opened and handed to the signed-in page (as Native's). The page no longer opens fk itself for such an account. rudolfd counts failures: after 5 wrong passwords or codes for an account, a wait (30 s, doubling to 15 min), recorded in System health; a security key needs no count (it is touched). The lock screen asks again (password and the second step; administrators may set "the key alone unlocks the lock screen while signed in").

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: 5. Requiring it. Security Settings › Sign-in: "Two-step sign-in: Not required / Required for administrators / Required for every account" (administrator, with its own password and second step to change it). An account that has none is signed in once more, then asked to add one before the desktop opens (a security key or codes; "Later" is not offered). The Guest account cannot have one and is turned off while "every account" is set. 6. The old page-checked keys. Accounts with one keep signing in on Standard as now; Settings shows "Set up again to protect your files and use Native and Lite" until the key is added again under item 1 (then the old one is removed).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: What it protects, said in Settings. A security key: someone who knows or guesses the password cannot sign in, and a copy of the disk is unreadable without a key. Codes: someone who knows the password cannot sign in at the screen. Not: someone with the computer while it is signed in and unlocked; that is the lock screen's job. Built in 1.6.0 (2026-11-19): items 3, 4 (in part) and 5; items 1, 2 and 6 later (the owner: "Codes now, keys after": security keys that unlock the files come in their own beta, tested first with a simulated key in QEMU and then the owner's real key, because a mistake there would lock people out of their own files).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: desktop/otp60.js: User Settings › Sign-in options › Authenticator app (Set up… with the setup key, base32, and the otpauth:// link; no QR code yet; a code and the password to confirm; Turn off, unless it is required); the code asked after the password at the sign-in screen (build19's sign-in patch, after the old page-checked security key) and at the lock screen; Security Settings › Two-step sign-in (Not required / administrators / every account; "every account" turns Guest off); an account that must and has none is asked to set it up after signing in, with Sign out and no "Later".

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: rudolfd (rudolfd-desktop.inc): the native sign-in and unlock ask for the code ({"need":"code"}, HTTP 401) after a right password and before anything is opened; desktop/second for the page; per account (second-ID): the last step used (a code is not taken twice) and wrong codes counted (5: 30 s, then doubling to 15 minutes). Wrong *passwords* on Standard are still counted by the page's own sign-in screen as before; on Native rudolfd's as before. rudolf-native: the second step in the same field ("Code from your authenticator app"), the password kept for it. Tests: iso/qt/host/totp60_t.sh (RFC 6238's values, rudolfd's and the page's), iso/qt/shell2/otp60_t.js (12), in otp-check.yml.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 17. Two-step sign-in, done properly (added on 2026-11-19)
docs.t: Tests (planned, for the keys). A virtual FIDO2 key (a CTAP2 HID device made with uhid, in QEMU) with hmac-secret and a PIN: adding two keys, signing in with either, the password-only copy gone (the disk image opened offline with the password fails, with a key's output it opens), wrong PIN and no key, the recovery code once, an administrator opening and resetting, the setting turned off; TOTP with the RFC 6238 test vectors, reuse refused, the waits; "required for every account" asking at the next sign-in; Standard, Native and Lite each signing in the same accounts.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 18. Security keys and the setup QR code: what Part 17 left (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: The owner, 2026-11-20: "Add everything else to 1.6.1." Part 17 was moved to 1.6.0 with "Codes now, keys after": the authenticator codes were built there (desktop/otp60.js, rudolfd's desktop/second); these were not. Security keys that unlock the files (Part 17 items 1, 2 and 6): a FIDO2 key's hmac-secret wraps the account's file key, so a copy of the disk needs the key as well as the password; two keys at least (a spare), rudolfd deciding (Part 17 item 4), Native and Lite accepting such accounts, the old page-only WebAuthn keys moved over.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 18. Security keys and the setup QR code: what Part 17 left (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: The setup QR code: User Settings › Sign-in options › Authenticator app shows the otpauth:// link as a QR code beside the setup key (an encoder of Rudolf's own in desktop/, as the commercial's: byte mode, levels M and Q, versions 1 to 10; checked by decoding it in the test), so a phone's app adds it with its camera. Tests: a simulated FIDO2 key in QEMU (as Part 17 planned) for the unlocking; the QR code decoded back to the link.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 19. Gaming on stronger computers (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: Asked on 2026-11-20 how Rudolf OS games on high-end hardware. Found then: AMD and Intel graphics use Mesa (close to Windows through Steam and Proton); NVIDIA cards have only NVK (iso/systools/addnvk.sh), well behind NVIDIA's own driver on recent GeForce cards (no DLSS frame generation, weaker ray tracing); no game mode; Standard's whole desktop stays behind a full-screen game. (The newest-kernel track and Wayland, for HDR and variable refresh, are docs/plan-2.0.md's.)

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 19. Gaming on stronger computers (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: NVIDIA's own driver, by choice: Settings › Display › Graphics driver: "Open (NVK)" (the default) or "NVIDIA's driver", for GeForce 16 and newer (the open kernel modules NVIDIA publishes), downloaded and signed for Secure Boot as a package from the Library with Rudolf's key, built in CI for the release's own kernel; switched back by itself (and said) when it fails to load, the recovery system always on the open driver.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 19. Gaming on stronger computers (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: A game mode: while a game is full screen, the CPU's energy preference raised (amd_pstate/intel_pstate), the desktop's own work paused (Standard's page throttled, the background jobs and Oracle's tabs held), notifications held; everything back as it was when the game leaves full screen. GameMode's requests from games honoured. gamescope comes with Wayland (2.0). Measured: the same games' frame rates and frame times on the open and NVIDIA drivers and with game mode on and off, on the owner's Asus desktop (live from a stick, as Part 12) and the Vivobook.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 20. Security hardening (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: From the comparison with other distributions on 2026-11-19: the weak points named then. rudolfd confined: an AppArmor profile (or, where AppArmor is not in the kernel, systemd-free equivalents: its capabilities limited, a seccomp filter) allowing only the paths and actions it uses; Part 11's helpers each with a narrower one; the page's API checked against a list of what each window may call. An outside security review: before 2.0, a review by people outside the project of rudolfd's API, the sign-in and encryption, the update and recovery chain and the development link; findings fixed, published with the release.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 20. Security hardening (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: Standard's website data, "off": a key sealed in the computer's TPM (bound to Secure Boot's measurements) in place of Chromium's built-in key, so a drive taken out cannot read the shared profile's cookies; written up with what it does not cover (the computer itself taken, signed-in use). From 1.6.0 Part 22's "could come later".

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 21. The checks that cannot run, and the checks with the owner (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: CI: the Oracle file check, the Tor window keys check and "same (beta)" fail on GitHub's runners because the beta's Chromium (chromium.sfs) does not start there ("required file not found", exit 127). Each moved to Playwright's Chromium as the newer checks were, or given the libraries the beta's Chromium needs, so every check runs again. A virtual smart card in QEMU (vsmartcard's reader with a PIV emulator and a test CA: 1.6.0 Part 20's planned test).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Parts › 21. The checks that cannot run, and the checks with the owner (added on 2026-11-20)
docs.t: On the Vivobook, with the owner: Oracle's websites encrypted (1.6.0 Part 22) on Native, Lite and Standard turned on; Recovery mode from a stick made from this release and from another build's; two-step sign-in on Standard and Native; calls; a real CAC only when the owner asks.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Not moved here
docs.t: Oracle's website data encrypted: written here on 2026-11-19, moved to 1.6.0 the same day (the owner: "Put it in 1.6.0 instead"): docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 22. elogind and polkit (1.6.0 Part 11): left out by decision on 2026-11-15, since Rudolf OS's own inhibit portal and prompts cover what apps ask. Taken up again only if an app or a later part needs them. Native as the default for new installations (#384): still 1.6.0's, for the owner's decision after the week of betas. The apps moved to native code: docs/plan-2.0.md. The phone's own interface (stage 2: the home screen's panels, the dialler, the lock screen, the shade, the touch layouts, Waydroid integrated, the camera and sensor apps): docs/plan-2.0.md, "The phone build".

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.1: what was moved out of 1.6.0 › Steps
docs.t: 1. Part 1, several monitors, after the 1.6.0 beta. 2. Part 3, Lite's leftovers, one PR each. 3. Part 8 (mobile data and the SIM on real hardware) with the MiFi, before the phone; Part 9 (USB printers; ARM64 with the phone or an ARM64 computer). 4. The phone's stage 1: Part 4 on the first phone (after 1.6.0's ARM64 release and stage B), Part 7 with a T-Mobile-network SIM, Part 6's 1.6.1 items measured on it, Part 2's groundwork; Part 5 when the hardware is there. 5. The phone's stage 2 (its interface, Wayland, the native apps for touch): docs/plan-2.0.md, "The phone build".

Part 15 (one title bar for apps that draw their own) with Part 14, before Native becomes the default: 2 first (the window manager's part), then 1 (the apps' own settings), then 3 (the per-app choice). 7. Part 16 (each other's builds): 1 and 2 first (the check and the beta switch), then 4's "kept newest", then 3 with 4's sticks (the stick from the address, always with the official recovery system). 8.
